item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 141722
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Mon Sep 14 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Norbert, located well east of the Hawaiian Islands, and on
Tropical Depression Fifteen-E, located several hundred
miles southwest of the southern tip of the Baja California
Peninsula.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

&&
Public advisories on Tropical Depression Fifteen-E are issued under
WMO header WTPZ35 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP5.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression Fifteen-E are issued
under WMO header WTPZ25 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP5.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Beven

500 AM HST Mon Sep 14 2026
 
...NORBERT HOLDING STEADY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 AM HST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.4N 137.8W
ABOUT 1125 MI...1810 KM E OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 280 DEGREES AT 15 MPH...24 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1005 MB...29.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM HST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Norbert was
located near latitude 19.4 North, longitude 137.8 West. Norbert is
moving toward the west near 15 mph (24 km/h) and is expected to
maintain this general motion during the next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 40 mph (65 km/h) with higher gusts.
A gradual weakening trend is forecast during the next couple of 
days, and Norbert could become a post-tropical cyclone tomorrow.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles (130 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1005 mb (29.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Bann/Blake

item.title: Tropical Storm Norbert Forecast Discussion Number 20
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Mon Sep 14 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 141437
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Norbert Discussion Number  20
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
Issued by the NWS Weather Prediction Center College Park MD
500 AM HST Mon Sep 14 2026
 
Deep convection, with cloud-top temperatures as cold as -80 C, has 
continued near and east of Norbert's center.  The center is on the 
southwestern edge of the convective mass due to shear.  Satellite 
intensity estimates have not changed in the past few hours, so the 
initial intensity is maintained at 35 kt.
 
The initial motion is estimated to be westward, or 280/13 kt. The
storm remains positioned south of a subtropical ridge, which should
continue to steer Norbert on a general west-northwestward to 
westward track until it dissipates in a few days. The track 
guidance remains in good agreement, and the NHC track forecast is 
basically an update of the previous one.
 
A combination of mid-level dry air and strengthening westerly
vertical wind shear should make it increasingly difficult for
Norbert to maintain organized deep convection, resulting in a steady
weakening trend over the next couple of days with the system 
expected to become post-tropical on Tuesday. The current NHC
intensity forecast is a little less than the previous one and shows 
Norbert dissipating as it opens into a trough by Wednesday.

MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1006 MB...29.71 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression
Fifteen-E was located near latitude 16.9 North, longitude 120.5
West. The depression is moving toward the west near 9 mph (15 km/h)
and this generally westward motion should continue for the next
several days with some increase in forward speed.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Some slight strengthening is forecast during the next 24 hours, and
the depression could become a tropical storm later today. The
system is expected to weaken beginning Tuesday night or Wednesday.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1006 mb (29.71 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.

-------------

$$

item.title: Tropical Depression Fifteen-E Forecast Discussion Number 5
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Mon Sep 14 2026 
682 
WTPZ45 KNHC 142035
TCDEP5
 
Tropical Depression Fifteen-E Discussion Number   5
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP152026
200 PM PDT Mon Sep 14 2026
 
Recent visible satellite imagery shows that the center of the
depression has become exposed and well removed from the convection
as northwesterly shear continues to push the convection away and
push dry air into the center of the cyclone. The center is also
farther north than previously thought. The current objective
intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS is in the range of 27-34 kt. As
such, the initial intensity has been kept at 30 kt.
 
Based on the more northward initial position, the depression is
moving west with an initial motion of 280/8 kt. The cyclone is being
steered by a ridge off to the northwest, and this ridge should
continue to be the main steering flow for the cyclone through the
forecast period. A general westward motion is expected to continue
with an increase in forward speed after 36-48 h. The current NHC
forecast track has been adjusted to the north of the previous track
and just a bit slower than before. The current forecast track is
closer to the HFIP Corrected Consensus Approach (HCCA) and Google
DeepMind (GDMI) forecast aids.
 
The environment is generally unfavorable for strengthening due to
the moderate northwesterly vertical wind shear advecting some dry
air into the center of the depression. However, the intensity
guidance shows the possibility of some strengthening during the next
24 h. As a result, the NHC intensity forecast calls for some slight
strengthening. While there is a period between 24-48 h where the
shear should weaken, the guidance suggests that the cyclone will not
be able to take advantage of this period to strengthen further.
After 48 h, the cyclone should weaken due to dry air entrainment
and eventual absorption into the larger monsoon trough. The NHC
intensity forecast is similar to the prior advisory, and is
slightly under the HCCA guidance for intensity.
